caption: A kite tied by its string to a fence post is lifted by a steady wind, and the string pulls taut from the post up to the kite.

sa.check: A kite is tied by a string to a fence post.
The kite is lifted into the air by the wind.
The string is taut from the post up to the kite.
The wind is steady and the kite holds rather than diving.
The lift comes first and the taut string follows.

pc.expect: The string runs in a shallow taut curve from post to kite and does not hang slack while the kite flies.
pc.fail: The string droops in loose loops while the kite is up; or it stretches; or it runs straight down from the kite to the ground with the kite still flying.

pc.expect: The kite is above the post with the string climbing from post to kite, and a slack string falls.
pc.fail: The kite is below the post with the string taut; or the string curves upward away from the kite; or the kite rises straight up and stays overhead with no lean downwind.

pc.expect: The string tugs at the post, and the post or the knot shows the pull.
pc.fail: The kite flies with the string not attached to anything; or the string is attached but the kite drifts away with it trailing; or the post pulls out of the ground.

pc.expect: The kite bobs and shifts with the wind but stays at the string's end and does not dart against the wind.
pc.fail: The kite flies upwind of the post; or it swoops in circles unrelated to the string; or it hovers with the string slack.

pc.expect: One kite, one string and one post keep their number.
pc.fail: The kite vanishes or a second appears; or the string passes through the post; or the kite turns into another object.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The kite's colours, the string and the fence stay the same.
pc.fail: The kite changes colour or shape; or the string changes; or the fence rearranges.
